name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joaquin Castro running with large fundraising edge
Republican challenger minimally funded and unknown
model.rationale: Castro is a well-funded incumbent in a D+16 San Antonio district, while Baez has raised under $50,000 and no outside spending or polls suggest any competitive dynamic. Markets price Castro at roughly 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in this heavily Democratic San Antonio district, where the partisan lean favors his party by about 16 points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over half a million dollars, while Republican Edgardo Baez has raised under $50,000 and reports modest cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price Castro's chances near certain. With no outside spending and no evidence of a competitive dynamic, the seat is rated Safe for Democrats, with an expected margin in the low twenties.
